company.name: Posy & Pail
company.tagline: A flower shop and a wedding workroom, with one Core on the back-office desk.
company.story: Posy & Pail is a florist with a workroom behind the shop. Ten people sell flowers, arrange weddings and keep the books. The orders, the supplier papers and the contracts sit on one Companion Core in the back office.

hookLine: The newsletter list sits on the Core, in the shop.
arc: The visual small business: a florist whose Core stands on a desk in the back office. Orders by phone and email, contracts at the consultation table, supplier papers scanned, the newsletter list kept in the shop. The person who "holds the list" owns the Core. Edge: no web shop, no online booking, no payments, no deliveries on screen; the van and the street are out of frame.
honestEdge: Nothing is sold, booked or paid online in these scenes. Orders come by phone and email, and the mail leaves through the provider the shop already uses.

building.concept: High-street brick terrace unit: glazed shop front with green awnings, a fascia strip (blank, no lettering), a closed neighbour unit (spike exists, reads as a shop from the street). Interior needs retail props (P2, about 3 d); fans off.

core.surface: desk (hero.surface: desk), chalk Core, no books
core.note: The contract's office-rooms rule must accept a Back Office holding the Core for retail (engine decision 4). 3.6 x 3.6 m minimum. The spike's back office reads as a home study: dress it as a desk with files and a printer.

building.route: double glazed door under the awning, Shop Floor, the Back Office door, orbit.

rooms.name: Shop Floor
rooms.note: wall shelving, display tables, cash counter near the door

rooms.name: Consultation Room
rooms.note: glass partition from the shop floor

objectProps: buckets of stems, wall shelving, a bench with recipe sheets, the consultation table, a green awning

lens.tone: Short dry bursts to peers, warm and exact with clients. Opens on a concrete noun.
lens.aiStance: Pragmatic. Wants drafts and answers from her own files. Proud of a chore done, not of having AI.
lens.honestLimit: No payroll, card processing or bank feeds; backup is the company's job; one Core is one owner's.

lens.tone: Practical, sceptical of gurus, short. "Who holds the list?"
lens.aiStance: Pragmatic, quietly pleased, careful who is told.
lens.honestLimit: Posts still go out to the platform; mail still leaves through a sender; no result, time or money claim.

companion.name: Pennant
companion.job: Drafts notes to growers and the shop's newsletter intro from what Katya types to it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Katya reads and sends every note.

lens.tone: Brisk, list-making, kind. Triages out loud. Humour about the printer.
lens.aiStance: Quiet user for notices and summaries. Not proud, not hiding. [?] no role survey
lens.honestLimit: Accounts are made app by app by whoever looks after each app; the Core is not a managed service.

lens.tone: Quick, numbers first, upbeat on the surface and dry underneath.
lens.aiStance: Heaviest adopter and proudest by reputation [?]; script slower than they talk.
lens.honestLimit: Reps away from the office are out of every scene; the CRM is the office's, not a per-rep platform account.

lens.tone: Exact, dry, deadline-led. Numbers are not adjectives.
lens.honestLimit: Bookkeeping tools, never accounting, tax or legal advice; no payroll, no bank feeds; never tell anyone to leave their accountant.

beats.title: A parcel between the buckets
beats.seed: A parcel waits inside the shop door, between the buckets. Olu carries it through the workroom to the back office, where Katya clears the desk.

beats.title: Unbox the Companion Core
beats.seed: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Rosa lifts the Core out, and Katya reads the guide.
beats.limit: Show exactly the box contents.

beats.title: Plug it in
beats.seed: Katya plugs in the cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.
beats.limit: note: Companion OS is in beta.

beats.title: Join it from a phone
beats.seed: Katya opens the Wi-Fi settings on her phone and joins the Core's own network. Then she chooses the shop network.
beats.limit: phone rows: Join the Core's own network; Choose the shop network; Enter its password

beats.title: Pick the first agent and apps
beats.seed: In the Companion Hub store, Katya picks Hermes, and the shop adds EspoCRM and Grist. Then the morning order gets placed.
beats.limit: note: Installing apps uses the internet.

beats.title: Pennant says hello
beats.seed: Katya messages the agent she named Pennant from the back office. Pennant answers from the Core on the desk beside her.
beats.limit: note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: katya
say.text: Hello, Katya. I draft the notes. You send them.

beats.capabilityHint: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick.

beats.title: Known trackers, blocked at the shop
beats.seed: Pi-hole blocks known ad and tracker domains for the devices pointed at it. Katya makes no promise beyond that.
beats.limit: No safety or protection promise. Blocks ad and tracker domains only. The package publishes DNS on port 8053, not 53: never say the shop network uses it or "answers the shop's name lookups". If the Core is off those devices lose lookups.
beats.capabilityHint: Block ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level.

beats.title: A note to the grower
beats.seed: Pennant drafts the standing-order note to the grower. Katya reads it, changes a line and sends it herself.
beats.limit: Agent prepares, person approves; contacting a supplier needs the approval in the beat. The channel is not local. No result claim.
beats.capabilityHint: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick.

beats.title: Supplier invoices, scanned
beats.seed: Maren scans the supplier invoices into Papra on the Core. A search for a grower's name finds every invoice in one list.
beats.limit: Write "Papra" exactly. PDFs and scans; no text-recognition quality claim. Email, the bank and the pay service stay with the services that run them.
beats.capabilityHint: Archive the receipts, warranties and contracts you rarely look at, until you need them.

beats.title: The hotel's monthly statement
beats.seed: Maren raises the monthly statement for the hotel account in Invoice Ninja. The statement is a PDF she prints and posts.
beats.limit: Invoicing, not payment processing; no card payments. Emailing needs SMTP. No ledger. Elastic License 2.0: never "open source".

bringHome.doesNot: the full books; the pay service; bank feeds

beats.capabilityHint: Send invoices and quotes, track expenses and time, and get paid.

beats.title: The week's order, one table
beats.seed: Olu keeps the week's flower order in a Grist table on the Core. Every grower has a column, and Monday's counts go in beside it.
beats.limit: Airtable import is Baserow's, not Grist's: say what was rebuilt. Grist is sentence-initial safe only as the app. In this Hub package Grist has one default sign-in (GRIST_DEFAULT_EMAIL) and no login provider: never per-person Grist accounts, never who sees which rows.

bringHome.carries: tables rebuilt by hand or by CSV; no importer claimed for Grist
bringHome.doesNot: automations and interfaces; row comments; revision history

beats.capabilityHint: A spreadsheet-database with real Python formulas, stored as a SQLite file you can copy.

beats.title: Monday's stem counts
beats.seed: On Monday Olu counts the stems by the cold door and types the counts into the same Grist table. Gaps show before the order goes.
beats.limit: Do not claim accuracy or waste reduction. No figure for money or time. In this Hub package Grist has one default sign-in (GRIST_DEFAULT_EMAIL) and no login provider: never per-person Grist accounts, never who sees which rows.
beats.capabilityHint: A spreadsheet-database with real Python formulas, stored as a SQLite file you can copy.

beats.title: The list sits on the Core
beats.seed: Katya keeps the shop's newsletter list in Listmonk on the Core. The mail itself leaves through the sender she picks.
beats.limit: Never promise delivery or opens. An SMTP provider is set inside the app. Mailchimp campaigns, templates and automations do not move.

bringHome.doesNot: campaigns and templates; automations and segments; reports; sending reputation starts again

beats.capabilityHint: Write and send newsletters to your own mailing list.

beats.title: Each wedding, one row
beats.seed: Eamon keeps every wedding enquiry in EspoCRM on the Core. Each couple has a row, a date and the notes from the tasting.
beats.limit: Web interface only. Enquiries arrive by phone and email: no booking page or public form. Never show a real-looking list.

bringHome.doesNot: automations and reports; sharing rules; activity history

beats.capabilityHint: Manage customers, sales pipelines, campaigns and support cases in a CRM you host.

beats.title: After the tasting, a note
beats.seed: After a tasting Eamon adds a note to the couple's row. The next call starts from what they chose.
beats.limit: Same app by design. No claim about conversion or results.
beats.capabilityHint: Manage customers, sales pipelines, campaigns and support cases in a CRM you host.

beats.title: The contract, signed at the table
beats.seed: Rosa and a couple sign the wedding contract at the consultation table. DocuSeal keeps the signed copy on the Core.
beats.limit: Never "legally binding" or "valid". The couple is in the room; signers outside the office cannot reach the Core.
beats.capabilityHint: Fill and sign PDF forms on any device, from your own Core.

beats.title: A quote, written while they choose
beats.seed: Eamon writes the wedding quote in Invoice Ninja while the couple choose. The quote sits on the Core with the contract.
beats.limit: No amounts anywhere. Invoicing, not payment processing.
beats.capabilityHint: Send invoices and quotes, track expenses and time, and get paid.

beats.title: The order of the day, typed
beats.seed: Eamon types the order of the day for the wedding in LibreOffice on the Core. A printed copy goes into the couple's folder.
beats.limit: One streamed desktop session, not co-editing. Name the suite, not features.
beats.capabilityHint: The LibreOffice suite (Writer, Calc and more) in your browser.

beats.title: The consultation diary
beats.seed: The consultation diary is a Baikal calendar the whole shop reads. Eamon adds each tasting, and nobody books the table twice.
beats.limit: A CalDAV client is the way in; invitations from outside people stay with the mail provider. Overlaps Radicale: name one. No public booking.

beats.capabilityHint: A small CalDAV and CardDAV server for your calendars and contacts.

beats.title: Each arrangement, a recipe sheet
beats.seed: Rosa writes each arrangement as a recipe sheet in LibreOffice. The printed sheet hangs above the bench while the stems go in.
beats.limit: Name the suite, not features. Layout can differ from Office files.
beats.capabilityHint: The LibreOffice suite (Writer, Calc and more) in your browser.

beats.title: The wedding week, on a board
beats.seed: Each wedding is a card on a Planka board above the workbench. Rosa moves it as the flowers arrive and the bouquets are done.
beats.limit: Trello JSON carries lists, cards, labels, checklists and comments; attachments and members unverified. Licence unasserted: never "open source".

bringHome.doesNot: Power-Ups and automations; attachments and members (check one board first)

beats.capabilityHint: A real-time Kanban board for a team or a family project.

beats.title: Delivery notes, filed by grower
beats.seed: Maren files each delivery note in Papra when the boxes come in. The paper copy goes in the stockroom tray.
beats.limit: Write "Papra" exactly. No claim about matching or checking.
beats.capabilityHint: Archive the receipts, warranties and contracts you rarely look at, until you need them.

beats.title: The delivery rota, by the kettle
beats.seed: The delivery rota is a Baikal calendar, and a printed copy hangs by the kettle. Olu changes it when a driver swaps a day.
beats.limit: The van and the roads are out of frame: only the rota is shown. No mobile or tracking claim.
beats.capabilityHint: A small CalDAV and CardDAV server for your calendars and contacts.

beats.title: The season, on one page
beats.seed: Katya lays the season out on one page in Companion Planning on the Core. Mother's Day and the wedding weeks get their time first.
beats.limit: An owner's planner, not a team calendar (one owner account). Google sync is off by default; do not say it never touches Google. Crash-report disclosure applies.
beats.capabilityHint: Plan tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core. Briefings from a local model are optional.

beats.title: Over to your shop
beats.seed: The orders, the supplier papers and the wedding contracts now sit on one desk in the back office. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.
beats.limit: closing body.

disclosuresRequired: synthetic-voice (when the tour has a voice)
writerRules: one person, one room, one app per beat; chip row is the app name then "replaces <service>" from the catalog entry
title at most six words, body at most thirty, sentence at most twenty, no digit, no dash, no exclamation mark, full stop
no UI mockup, no screen described, no customer, no price, no result, no time or capacity claim
the agent prepares and a person approves; one companion, on the Core's owner
every scene stays in the building on the office network; no remote, hybrid, mobile, public link or client portal
per-app accounts only, named as that app's own feature; never a Companion account per person
say what did not come along in every bring-your-data-home beat
sentence case; sign in, not log in; agent, not assistant; Companion Core, Companion Hub store

a file moves between apps by a person's hand (download, copy, file it), never by an integration: LibreOffice, Inkscape, Stirling-PDF, BentoPDF and draw.io keep nothing on the Core; never "goes straight into", "syncs to" or "lands in" another app (skeptic)
Hermes runs isolated from the other apps: it works from what a person types or pastes to it, never from a repository, a wiki or a drive it "reads" (skeptic)

capabilityHint strings are the catalog's own words and are never scanned by the validator: do not paste them into a title, body, caption or note; they hold words the canon bans (private, sandbox, QR code, bot API, nothing is uploaded, not sent to a third party, stays on your Core) (skeptic)
no sentence puts a head count and the Core together as "N people on one Core"; the Core belongs to one owner and the apps keep their own sign-ins (skeptic)
a replaces chip is the store's own pair; where a beat below carries no chip it is deliberate (skeptic: Uptime Kuma, Cryptgeon and LibreOffice pairs the briefs' own limits contradict)

changes: tagline: "Ten people ... on one Core" put a head count and the Core together; reworded
back-dns: same Pi-hole correction as Gutterfold; title "The shop's name lookups" -> "Known trackers, blocked at the shop"
Grist one-sign-in limit and the Planka licence note added

hook line and titles: "stay in the office/studio/shop" is a place claim wider than the canon's "sits on the Core" (and a sent newsletter hands its addresses to the mail provider); now "sit on the Core"
unverified: Listmonk subscriber consent: a moved list carries addresses, not proof of consent; no beat claims otherwise
Papra cut chips "replaces Evernote, replaces Google Drive" are the store's pairs but the market review calls them a loose fit: O13
